column1: # The file device's traces: what its runtime's end owes a core (abi/fs.json, ipc/fs.json,
# ARCHITECTURE.md's files), apart from the boundary's rules C0 to C7 — the boundary
# carries the calls, and this is what they mean. Run against the runtime's end
# (ts/runtime/src/ipc/fs.test.ts): a step writes a record as a core's turn would, `turn`
# runs them as the runtime does after a turn, and what reaches the core is held to the trace.
#   file R P B        the runtime's file P below root R: its bytes in hex, ENOENT, or `later` —
#                     answered only when a `deliver` says, as a transport answers
#   openat FD R F P   a core's OPENAT: FD as the core issued it (slot and generation), F rd or wr,
#                     P the path, `""` for an empty one
#   read FD N / write FD TEXT / close FD
#   turn              the runtime runs the turn's records
#   deliver R P B     the transport answers what `later` held, with B as `file` takes it
#   expect opened FD RES   the next completion the core is sent, of an open: a size, or an errno by name
#   expect closed FD RES   the next, of a close: 0, or an errno by name
#   expect quiet      no completion the core has not been held to
#   expect read HEX   what the last read put in the core's memory
#   expect commit R P TEXT   what a close made the file
# An open's completion comes on a later turn, however much later: `later` is how a trace says the
# transport is slow, and nothing here fixes how many turns pass. Each open and each close is

column1: # A read of a descriptor this runtime does not hold, as the one a reload replaced left in the ring,
# is dropped, and its close says so.
# Opened to write and closed in one turn: an open to write is completed at once, and the close
# commits what was written, read where the core keeps it.
# A file refused to write is written and closed in the same turn: the write is dropped, the open
# completed with its errno, and the close finds no descriptor.
# A close ends a descriptor still opening: its open is completed with ECANCELED before the close,
# and nothing more, however late its transport.
# A close of a descriptor the runtime does not hold is completed with EBADF.
# The slot a closed descriptor held is issued again under a new generation before the old open's
# transport answers: the old open is completed with ECANCELED at its close, the late answer reaches
# neither descriptor, and the new one gets its own.
# A root is the whole of what it grants: a path walks down from it a name at a time, and a name
# that is empty, `.` or `..` — an absolute path's first among them — is refused before any runtime sees it.
